clue.text: Composer in street fumin' against the heavens

parts.note: fuming, with its last letter dropped, is raving with its G dropped too: ravin'
the sky is the heavens above

explanation.surface: A composer stands in the road raging at the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in "fumin'" tells you to drop the final G of its synonym, raving.
explanation.definitionFit: Igor Stravinsky was the Russian-born writer of The Rite of Spring.

clue.text: Fish unhappy having caught tip of hook

indicators.note: having caught means the first word holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: unhappy means sad

indicators.note: the tip of a word here is its first letter, from the word hook

explanation.surface: An angler's fish looks miserable with a hook in its mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: The shad is a herring-like sea fish that swims upriver to spawn.

clue.text: Agent in borders of Ecuador, one feeling discontent

parts.note: a rep, short for representative, is a sales agent
taken as written

indicators.note: the borders of a word are its first and last letters, here from Ecuador

explanation.surface: A sales agent stuck on the Ecuadorian frontier is unhappy with his lot.
explanation.definitionFit: To repine is to fret or complain, so someone who does so is a malcontent.

clue.text: ITV — Mary chats about students' game

indicators.note: about signals that the letters of these words are moved around

explanation.surface: Mary talks about the TV channel ITV.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges ITV, MARY and CHATS. A varsity match is an annual sports fixture between Oxford and Cambridge universities.
explanation.definitionFit: A varsity match is a contest between university teams, most famously Oxford against Cambridge at rugby.

clue.text: Observing what novel form of cake topping is!

definitions.text: what novel form of cake topping is!

explanation.surface: Someone spotting a cake with an unusual topping.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer into two words: a new kind of cake topping is, by definition, something other than the usual sugar coating.
explanation.definitionFit: Observing means seeing or spotting; and a novel topping is one that is not the familiar sugary coating on a cake.

clue.text: Some coins with two kings, and one with one!

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king, and R (rex, Latin) is the other
R stands for rex, Latin for king
taken as written
the first one is one more king, R for rex

explanation.surface: Coins depicting two kings, and one coin showing just one king.
explanation.walkthrough: Kings come as K and R (rex). The answer is K and R, then ONE with another R: four pieces, three of them kings.
explanation.definitionFit: Kroner are the currency units of Denmark and Norway.

clue.text: Obstinate, not half, when producing short piece

indicators.note: not half means the word for obstinate loses half its letters, here the back half

parts.note: obstinate means stubborn

explanation.surface: Someone stubborn only goes halfway when making something short.
explanation.definitionFit: A stub is a short leftover piece, like a cigarette end or a ticket counterfoil.

clue.text: Administer corporal punishment to man for touching

parts.note: to tan someone's hide is to beat them
a gent is a man

explanation.surface: Thrashing a man for touching something he shouldn't.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'tan' someone is informal for giving them a beating.
explanation.definitionFit: Tangent means meeting a curve at one point, so it is touching, the sense of the Latin root.

clue.text: Messy cow by steed in Welsh village

indicators.note: messy signals that the letters of these words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A dirty cow stands beside a horse in a Welsh village.
explanation.definitionFit: Betws-y-Coed is a tourist village in Snowdonia in north Wales.

clue.text: Flying into Paris, a thing one would like to do?

definitions.text: thing one would like to do?

indicators.note: flying signals that the letters of these words take off into a new order

explanation.surface: Flying into Paris is something you would like to do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' looks like a link word but is part of what 'Flying' rearranges: INTO, PARIS and A.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspiration is a hope or ambition, something you long to achieve.

clue.text: Insect of annoying nature

indicators.note: of means the answer is made up of letters inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: An insect with an irritating character.
explanation.definitionFit: The gnat is a small two-winged fly, often biting.

clue.text: Number of hospital patients, might you say?

definitions.text: Number of hospital patients, might you say?

parts.words: Number of hospital patients, might you say?
parts.note: read number as someone who numbs: the medical specialist who makes patients numb before surgery

explanation.surface: A question about how many patients a hospital holds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' looks like a count, but read it as one who numbs.
explanation.definitionFit: This doctor administers drugs that remove feeling, so jokingly is a numb-er of patients.

clue.text: One backing a national organisation or voting against?

indicators.note: backing means the piece for one comes at the back, after the others

parts.note: NT is the National Trust, a British heritage charity
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A supporter of a national body, or someone opposed to it?
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' looks like support, but says I goes at the back. The National Trust looks after historic houses and land in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is anti is opposed, so this is a vote against a proposal.

clue.text: Detergents that could bring clearness

indicators.note: could bring signals that the letters of the following word can be rearranged to produce the answer

explanation.surface: Washing products that make things clear.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleansers are cleaning agents, like soaps and washing powders.

clue.text: Defeat those running the company? Just the ticket!

parts.note: to paste is slang for thrashing or beating soundly
a company's directors form its board

explanation.surface: Beating the directors would be just the thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just the ticket' looks like an idiom for 'ideal'; here it is literal: a ticket made of stiff card.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasteboard is stiff card, the stuff old railway tickets were made of.

clue.text: Adorning man in a piece of jewellery

indicators.note: in means the man's name goes inside the word for jewellery

parts.note: a ring is a piece of jewellery
Ray is a man's name

explanation.surface: Decorating a man inside a jewel.
explanation.definitionFit: To array is to dress or deck out, so arraying is decorating someone finely.

clue.text: The man with cold, twitching and feverish

parts.note: he is the man
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
a tic is a nervous twitch

explanation.surface: A man with a cold, shaking and running a temperature.
explanation.definitionFit: Hectic once meant a fever with flushed cheeks, as with tuberculosis, before it came to mean frantic.

clue.text: Organ's apt to go wrong — not ace rendering melody

indicators.note: to go wrong signals that the letters are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: the possessive gives no letter, just organs
taken as written
A is the abbreviation for ace on playing cards

explanation.surface: An organ likely to malfunction, and without its star player, while performing a tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go wrong' jumbles ORGANS and APT; 'not ace' says one A is left out of the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: A part-song is a tune for several voices singing in harmony, a kind of melody.

clue.text: Army's fellow becoming famous navigator

parts.note: the TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve; with the possessive it is TA's
a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: A soldier from the reserve army goes on to become a celebrated explorer.
explanation.walkthrough: The TA, Territorial Army, was Britain's part-time volunteer reserve force.
explanation.definitionFit: Abel Tasman was the Dutch explorer after whom Tasmania is named.

clue.text: One of tools in box — nine in it, one missing

indicators.note: in it means the trimmed number goes inside the word for box

parts.note: to spar is to box

indicators.note: missing means a letter is left out of the word nine

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A tool in the toolbox, with nine in there and one gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' takes I out of NINE, leaving NNE; 'in it' puts that inside SPAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A spanner is a wrench, one of a set of tools for turning nuts.

clue.text: Something sung in church is able to please, they say

indicators.note: they say means the words are spoken and heard, not spelt

parts.note: is able means can, and to please or amuse is to tickle

explanation.surface: A church hymn that manages to delight the congregation.
explanation.definitionFit: A canticle is a hymn or chant with a biblical text, like the Magnificat.

clue.text: Atmospheric conditions and so on upset round capital city

indicators.note: round means the turned letters go around the capital
in a down clue, upset means the letters are turned bottom to top

parts.note: etc is the abbreviation for et cetera, and so on
Lima is the capital of Peru

explanation.surface: Weather and such things cause trouble in a capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns ETC into CTE; 'round' wraps that around LIMA.
explanation.definitionFit: Climate is the typical weather of a region over a long period.

clue.text: Have a breather in gym or else swim

indicators.note: in means the breathing organ goes inside the letters for gym

parts.note: PE is physical education, school gym class
a lung is what you breathe with

explanation.surface: Take a rest at the gym, or else go swimming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breather' looks like a rest; it is the organ you breathe with.
explanation.definitionFit: A plunge is a quick dip or dive into water.

clue.text: A little bit wooden?

parts.note: read literally: a small offshoot of a tree, not a stiff or awkward manner

explanation.surface: A remark that someone's acting was somewhat stiff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wooden' looks like stilted acting, but means made of wood: a small piece of tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A small twig growing from a larger bough of a tree.

clue.text: This boy's turned green

indicators.note: turned means the word for green is read backwards

parts.note: lime is a shade of green

explanation.surface: This lad has gone green, perhaps from envy.
explanation.definitionFit: Emil is a boy's name, as in Emil and the Detectives.

clue.text: Galas losing little time making money

definitions.note: plural payments defined by a mass noun

indicators.note: losing means a letter is taken out of the word for galas

parts.note: fetes are galas or fairs
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Galas that run short of time still make a profit.
explanation.definitionFit: Fees are charges paid for services, sums of cash.

clue.text: Relation making excursion heading off

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter of the word for excursion is removed

parts.note: a jaunt is a short excursion

explanation.surface: A relative sets off on a trip.
explanation.definitionFit: An aunt is a parent's sister, a family member.

clue.text: Cause to get drunk bringing extraordinary excitation

indicators.note: extraordinary signals that the letters of excitation are put into an unusual order

explanation.surface: Getting someone drunk brings remarkable excitement.
explanation.definitionFit: To intoxicate is to make inebriated with alcohol.

clue.text: Striding back, find some muck

indicators.note: back means the letters taken are read in reverse order
some means only part of the word striding is used

explanation.surface: Walking back with long steps, you find mud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes TRID from Striding; 'back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Dirt is filth or grime, mud on your boots.

clue.text: Not finding our planet attractive?

parts.note: read attractive literally: not pulled by Earth's gravity, as in space

explanation.surface: Someone who dislikes the world we live on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'attractive' looks like a matter of taste; it is gravitational pull.
explanation.definitionFit: In orbit astronauts have no apparent heaviness because gravity no longer seems to pull them.
